items.title: Breaking Your Mortgage Early in a Spousal Buyout: How Prepayment Penalties Work
items.summary: Most spousal buyouts mean breaking your current mortgage, and the penalty can run into five figures. This guide explains the two ways lenders usually charge it: three months’ interest, and the interest rate differential (IRD), which is based on the gap between your rate and today’s rates. It works through an example with real numbers, then covers who pays the penalty and four ways you may be able to lower it.Want to build the penalty into your plan? items.title: Spousal Buyout Mortgages: Can You Borrow More Than 80% of Your Home’s Value?
items.summary: A regular refinance usually stops at 80% of your home’s value. That can leave you short when you’re buying out your spouse. Some insured spousal buyout programs let you borrow up to 95%. This guide works through an example with real numbers. It covers the mortgage insurance premium and the Ontario sales tax on it, the stress test you still have to pass, and the paperwork lenders want before you apply.Want to see how much you’d need to borrow? items.title: Appraisal or Online Estimate: What Is the House Really Worth in a Spousal Buyout?
items.summary: An online estimate and a professional appraisal can be tens of thousands of dollars apart. In a spousal buyout, every $10,000 of difference moves the payment by $5,000. This guide follows one Ontario couple through three different values for the same house, explains which date the value should be based on, and shows three ways separating spouses can agree on one fair number.Want to see what your own buyout would cost? items.title: Land Transfer Tax and Legal Fees on a Spousal Buyout in Ontario
items.summary: Keeping the house after separation? In Ontario, a transfer of the home between spouses is often exempt from land transfer tax, but only if it’s set up the right way. This guide explains the three ways to qualify, the costs you’ll still pay to transfer title and refinance, and how to keep a mortgage penalty from eating into your buyout. It uses a worked example with real numbers.Want to see what your own buyout would cost?
